text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentCan Science Save the Ice Skaters?Geoengineers have an ingenious plan to rescue the world’s most famous ice-skating race from global warmingTBBy Tim Brinkhof11:00 AM CST on November 18, 2026Add Nautilus to Google“It giet oan,” Henk Kroes, veteran “ice master,” told a room full of reporters on January 2, 1997: “It is happening.”Kroes was referring to the Elfstedentocht, a 125-mile ice skating competition in the northern Netherlands province of Friesland. For more than a century, the race has been as much a competition as a national celebration. “Never am I happier,” wrote the 17th-century playwright and skating enthusiast Gerbrand Bredero, “as when I am gliding over ice.” The feeling was passed down over the ages in the Netherlands.This story is from “The Hot Issue,” the latest from Nautilus.To get it in print, join by Nov 30.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
